resolved.answer: Same study, different cut. Rhodium's own note gives ranges (5-148 Mt in 2040; $50-78 per household; 17-249 GW). Heatmap and MIT Technology Review report the high end of each range, which Rhodium labels its best case. Not a misreport; the low ends are the other scenario.

Neither figure is on either primary page. RFF gives about 200 Mt near term, about 1.8 Gt cumulative to 2041 (and 107 Mt in 2041 in the detail). SEIA gives about 20% cumulative power-sector CO2 over 2028-2035 and a page-level caveat on absolute magnitudes. Breakthrough's per-year numbers are unreproducible and no derivation is stated. They are not published as estimates.

resolved.topic: ACP: pv magazine 'roughly 200 GW' vs 350+ GW
resolved.answer: ACP's own fact-sheet page (uploaded Oct 9, 2026) says 350+ GW of new clean energy, over $800 billion and 290 Mt avoided CO2 per year, with no scenario or baseline. The 200 GW in pv magazine is not on that page; it may come from a different ACP document that was not located. The ACP page figures are published as ACP's, scenario 'not stated'.

resolved.topic: Columbia '~100 GW by 2035' vs C2ES/Greenline 170 GW
resolved.answer: Columbia's white paper cites 'some estimates' for about 100 GW without naming a study, so it is a secondary citation and is not published. C2ES/Greenline's own release says 170 GW of added wind, solar and storage by 2035.

resolved.topic: Different studies, same bill: units and scope
resolved.answer: Rhodium (economy-wide, 2040, three provision groups), RFF (power sector, ReEDS, through 2041, power-sector provisions), C2ES/Greenline (power sector, 2035, interconnection and transmission), SEIA (power sector, cumulative 2028-2035, obstructed-permitting baseline) and CEA (GDP from review-time cuts) measure different things. No figure was averaged, converted or combined.
